clue.text: Grew fashionable fruit

parts.note: grew in the sense of went up or increased, past tense rose
hip is slang for trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Something got trendy and turned into a fruit, like an orchard keeping up with fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod left on a wild rose bush after flowering is a fruit, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: Celebrity concerned with new gown goes topless

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: topless means the top letter of gown is removed, in a down answer the first

explanation.surface: A star preoccupied with a new frock ends up wearing nothing on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame or wide acclaim is what a celebrated person enjoys.

clue.text: Just then, left city in Cambridgeshire

parts.note: so means then, as in so we left
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Someone simply left a Cambridgeshire city, and that was that.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and merely are synonyms, as in just one or exclusively one.

clue.text: Workmanship shown by sailor on current vessel

parts.note: a hand is a crew member on a ship
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a craft is a boat or ship

explanation.surface: A sailor shows good skill aboard a ship that is still in service.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled manual making of objects, such as pottery or weaving, is craftsmanship.

clue.text: Analyse sample from feldspar seam

indicators.note: sample from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A geologist examines a specimen taken from a vein of feldspar mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a sentence into its grammatical parts is to analyse it.

clue.text: Arrogant poster might be this

definitions.meaning: snooty, conceited, looking down on others
a poster is fixed in place on a wall, pasted up high

explanation.surface: A haughty person is compared to a bill pasted on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means snobbish as an idiom, and literally describes a notice glued up on a hoarding.

clue.text: Son walked away, dazed

parts.note: paced means walked up and down
out means away, as in she is out

explanation.surface: A son wandered off in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disoriented and vacant, as if drugged, is to be in a stupor.

clue.text: Almost join detachment

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is not reached

parts.note: to unite is to join together

explanation.surface: Someone nearly joins up but stays aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detachment' suggests aloofness, but it is a military sense: a group of troops sent off on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a body of soldiers detailed for a task, a military formation.

clue.text: Play golf with poet — putting mostly agreeable at the start

indicators.note: putting here means placing, so the shortened synonym is being set down somewhere
at the start says the shortened synonym goes in front of the other pieces
mostly means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: kind means pleasant or agreeable
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Edward Lear was a poet of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A round of golf with a poet, his putting mostly pleasant early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' looks like golf on the green, but it means placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about an old monarch and his three daughters is a stage drama.

clue.text: I will struggle with degree under pressure and strain

indicators.note: in a down answer under means the scrambled letters sit below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: struggle suggests writhing about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A student fears failing a degree under pressure and strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but it is a breed or line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a line of breeding, and a recorded ancestry of an animal is its lineage.

clue.text: Tailor only after northern fabric

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the abbreviation for northern
to tailor is to cut and reshape, so the letters of only are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tailor is asked to work only with cloth from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synthetic polymer woven into stockings and other textiles, so a man-made material.

clue.text: Put straight troubled Geraldine

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sorted out a woman named Geraldine who was in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring back into line is to set things straight again, as with wheels or teeth.

clue.text: You don't say very much at home at any time

parts.note: well as an intensifier, as in well pleased, means very much
in means at home, as in staying in
ever means at any time, as in have you ever

explanation.surface: Someone is told they rarely speak, very much at home whenever.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, idioms used when hearing something astonishing.

clue.text: Golfer aims for this standard

definitions.meaning: on a golf course the pin on each green carries a small banner the player targets
a standard is a banner or ensign carried on a pole

explanation.definitionFit: A banner is called a standard in military use, and a golf green's pin bears one as its target marker.

clue.text: Upper-class rogue helps — Tory seat might need this

indicators.note: rogue means wayward or out of control, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: A posh scoundrel helps a Conservative in a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory seat' reads as a parliamentary constituency, but the Tory goes into the anagram and the seat is a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair or sofa needs padding, springs and cloth covering, the soft furnishing on furniture.

clue.text: Group of big cats from Portugal mix in prominent position

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
to lace a drink is to mix a spirit into it

explanation.surface: Lions from Portugal are blended into a spot at the top of the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the most honoured spot, such as the central place on a mantelpiece.

clue.text: Knitting clothes endlessly, and making what Olympian Daley was best at?

definitions.text: what Olympian Daley was best at?

indicators.note: knitting interweaves strands, so the letters are woven together anew
endlessly means the last letter of clothes is cut off

explanation.surface: A knitter makes clothes nonstop, a hint at what a famous Olympian excelled at.
explanation.walkthrough: Daley Thompson was a British athlete who won Olympic gold in 1980 and 1984. 'endlessly' trims clothes to CLOTHE, mixed with AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Thompson's event was the ten-discipline athletics contest, so his speciality.

clue.text: I am above ancient city in China that's undeveloped

indicators.note: in a down answer above means the contraction sits on top

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: in says the city goes inside the synonym for china

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be above an old city in China that has not yet developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is rhyming slang (china plate for mate), a London usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Unripe or childish, not fully grown, means not yet developed.

clue.text: Adores words from groom, maybe — stories about stables, primarily

parts.note: a bridegroom says I do at the wedding

indicators.note: about means the lies wrap around the letter

parts.note: lies are false stories

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of stables

explanation.surface: A groom, perhaps in a stable rather than at a wedding, tells tales and adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' and 'stables' suggest horses, but the groom is a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone as a hero is to adore them deeply.

clue.text: Coins of a timid criminal — no small change

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted round
no says the letter for small must be absent from the fodder

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A timid crook's coins are described, with no small change among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes S out of COINSOFATIMID, leaving COINOFATIMID, which 'criminal' rearranges. 'small change' looks like loose coins, but only 'change' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration or adjustment to something is a change made to it.

clue.text: Woman departs in the morning — she leaves husband with student

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
a.m. means in the morning

indicators.note: leaves means she goes without the husband's letter

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver's plate, so a student

explanation.surface: A woman walks out one morning, abandoning her husband for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a young unmarried woman or maiden.

clue.text: Independent politician taken in by broadcasting company? That's revealing

indicators.note: taken in by means these letters go inside the broadcaster

parts.note: Sky is a UK broadcasting company
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An independent MP is duped by a TV company in an exposé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing' seems to mean an exposé, but it describes scanty clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing shows a lot of skin, so it is revealing.

clue.text: Intelligent former Liberal Democrat leader caught out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for caught is taken away

parts.note: Sir Vince Cable led the UK Liberal Democrats from 2017 to 2019
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A clever ex-party leader has been caught out, as politicians often are.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party; Vince Cable was their leader. 'caught out' reads as one phrase but means remove C.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable and competent is close to being clever or smart.

clue.text: Anxiety with boy's accent

parts.note: stress is worry or anxiety
Mark is a boy's name; the 's reads as the boy's name joining on

explanation.surface: A worried lad with a distinctive way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' looks like a regional voice, but here it is the written sign over a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent in writing is the symbol that shows which syllable takes emphasis.

clue.text: Two European articles for church official

parts.note: the clue offers two European definite articles; the first is el, the Spanish word for the
the second article is der, the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Two items from Europe are written up for a church dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches an elder is a lay officer who helps govern the congregation.

clue.text: Quiet and poorly? This may help

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
ill means poorly or unwell

explanation.surface: A quiet word to someone feeling unwell: this will help.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet of medicine is a remedy that may make a sick patient better.

clue.text: Manual taken out after confusion finally divides us

indicators.note: after places the synonym for taken out behind the rest
divides means a letter splits the pair of letters in us

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of confusion

parts.note: to take out someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: An instruction manual got lost after a muddle split the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' looks like a handbook noun but is the adjective, as in manual labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual work is labour by hand needing no special training, so without trained expertise.

clue.text: Where one might find better sheep — some pens

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the words sheep some hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A farmer's guide to where superior sheep are kept in pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is not the comparative of good but one who bets. EPSOM in Surrey has a famous racecourse, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse town is where a gambler on horses would be found at the races.

clue.text: Greek character records lion, one moving west

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the letter shifts towards the front of lion

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Records featuring a lion, one heading west, sound like a Greek tale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: King, perhaps, writing payment for Queen?

definitions.meaning: a king is an example of the monarch's family and class
the band Queen earn fees from their songs being used, a writer's share of sales

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers kings and queens collectively, and also a fee paid to an author per copy sold.
